findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Overall, the PIC failed to perform basic managerial duties within the establishment. There are many priority/priority foundation violations observed during today’s visit. Cold holding temperatures were observed noncompliant. The ambient temperature of the kitchen was roughly 90F due to the air conditioning failing. There is a presence of live (and dead) insects on food and non food contact surfaces, many foods are unlabeled and not date marked, and the cleanliness of the place is lacking. SCDPH will schedule an educational visit in the near future. Discussed active managerial control duties with manager to enforce with staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(B) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (B) Being a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Throughout the duration of the inspection, no handwashing was observed by any of the food employees. Employees should be washing hands frequently, including when switching tasks, and between each glove switch. Ensure to discuss proper handwashing with all food employees.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(A) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wash their hands as specified under § 2-301.12.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the hand sink within the dish area. Discussed with the PIC and soap was provided to the sink to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always hand soap available at all hand sinks to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was a dead roach observed inside of a salt container stored within the service station. Shown to the PIC and the container was discarded. Ensure that food is protected with coverings and also rotated frequently to be sure that old foods are being used first. Because there is a presence of insect activity, foods and food contact surfaces should always be protected and stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The shelves that stores clean dishes in the dish area contained at least three dead insects on the shelving surface. No insects were observed on the dishes, however, the shelves shall be maintained clean and free of insects. Ensure to remove dishes from shelf to be re-cleaned and also clean shelves before returning dishes. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 to see that shelves have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility lacks proper date marking. Many time/temperature foods (TCS) were observed without date marking. These items includes cooked meats, rice, sauces, cut melons, etc. Discussed the need to date mark TCS foods that will be held in house longer than 24 hours. Ensure that foods are date marked to be sure that foods are used within the seven day timeframe. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 too see that TCS foods are date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: The facility serves sushi and it appears that there is not a policy in place to control the safety of the sushi rice. There is only a small portion that is prepared at a time, however, the facility doesn’t follow a specific policy for safety reasons of the rice. Rice was observed covered and unlabeled. The PIC indicated that rice is being held on the counter to cool down and will be placed inside of the cooler at night. Discussed the need to either use time control for the rice or acidification. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 to put a plan into action for monitoring the safety of the rice.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The walk in cooler appears to not be functioning properly. Soup and a mayonnaise based sauce were probed at 53F. The hanging thermometers read between 58F-60F. The cooler is storing various foods including cut veggies, meats, soups, sauces, noodles, etc. The PIC mentioned that facility will contact a service technician to fix the cooler tomorrow. Ensure that cooler is adequate enough to maintain temperatures of 41F or below. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 to see that the cooler has been serviced and is holding cold holding temps of 41F or less.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: There was an abundance of foods stored within the facility that lacked proper labeling. Some foods were removed from the original container and could not be easily identified. These foods were stored in many areas of the facility including, inside coolers, on top of counters, in the dry storage area, etc. Ensure to label foods that aren’t visibly recognizable so that they are easily identified.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were at least five live roaches on the floor behind the cookline. The insects observed were fast moving and on the run. Shown to the PIC and she indicated that Orkin usually treats the premise monthly. The most recent receipts were from July 2026. Discussed the need to have pest service more frequent to reduce insect activity. Ensure that the premise is maintained free of roaches. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 check on insect activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood system were observed heavily accumulated with dried grease. The facility contracts Steam Power to service their hood system. Discussed with the PIC that baffles should be cleaned in house in between professional cleanings. Steam power last serviced the hood on May 17, 2026. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The facility overall is completely cluttered. There are various personal items mixed in with items intended for public consumption. These areas include shelves within the dry storage area, walk in units, and the service area. Discussed the need to remove unnecessary items from the premise if nonfunctional or if its doesn’t pertain to the operations of the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The facility could use some deep cleaning. The following areas are as followed: floor and wall behind cook-line line, shelving that stores clean dishes and food, ceilings, floors, and walls throughout the kitchen and dish area. There’s mainly an accumulation of food debris and dried grease on the above mentioned surfaces. Additionally, be sure to especially clean behind cook-line, as this is the area where live roaches were observed. The cove base has also pulled away from the wall behind the cookline. Be sure to reseal cove base back to wall and thoroughly clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed engaging in food prep without washing hands. The employee recently entered the facility from outdoors and went to the cookline to handle food. Discussed with the PIC proper handwashing and the need of washing hands when entering from outside. Ensure to always wash hands before engaging in food prep if tasks are interrupted.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed a container of raw chicken stored on the counter at room temperature. The PIC mentioned that the employees were going to portion the chicken into smaller batches. Discussed that chicken shall stay in cold holding equipment until it’s ready for use. The tub of chicken was placed inside of the walk in cooler to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods maintain proper cold holding temperatures at 41F or below when not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
findings.comment: The facility prepares and serves sushi in house made with both raw and cooked seafood. There wasn’t a consumer advisory sign posted throughout the facility making consumers aware of the health risks, nor is there a disclaimer on the menu. A consumer advisory sign was posted for customers’ view to correct the violation. Be sure to work on adding a disclaimer to the menu to make consumers aware of the health risks associated with the consumption of raw or undercooked foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were several mouse dropping on the floor surrounding the water heater in the main kitchen area. Shown to the PIC and the droppings were cleaned to correct the violation. No other droppings were observed throughout the facility. Discussed cleaning in hard to reach areas, as well as areas that don’t get used very often to prevent harboring conditions for pest (in addition to cleaning heavily used areas). Ensure that the premises is free of insects and regularly cleaned to eliminate the presence of unwanted pest.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The containers that the facility uses for storing ready-to-eat (RTE) foods aren’t food grade approved. The containers have many cracks, aren't durable, and will not be able to withstand repeated ware washing. Discussed with the PIC that containers for storing food must be sufficient in thickness and resistant to cracking and tares. In the near future, purchase containers that are food grade approved if using to store food in house. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The main cook’s food handler certificate has expired. The PIC mentioned that the facility will have the employee’s certificate renewed. Ensure that any employee who cooks or handles clean dishes obtain either a food handler certificate or a food manager certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Inspector observed raw pork being stored over cooked food. Discussed with PIC, and (CORRECTED) PIC moved the raw pork underneath the cooked food. Ensure that meat is stored in correct order to prevent cross-contamination. 

(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Three areas were observed in need of painting or refinishing:

-The ramp on the floor going into the kitchen area needs repainted. The old paint has worn away, allowing the bare wood underneath to show.

-The cart in the kitchen is rusted and dirty. Ensure the cart is cleaned and repainted to keep the surface clean, smooth, and durable.

-One side of the triple sink has a rusted metal plate on it. Ensure this area is cleaned and refinished or repainted to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. The shelf above the sink needs cleaned as well.

-The triple sink now has several gaps where caulking is needed. Ensure that all gaps in the metal on the triple sink are caulked.

findings.comment:

All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods. 

Observed employee rinse hands in handsink without soap, and turn off faucet with bare hands. Discussed proper handwashing procedure with PIC. Steps include: turn on water, get paper towels ready for drying, apply soap to hands, lather and scrub all areas of hands for at least 20 seconds, rinse off hands, use paper towels to dry hands, use paper towel to turn off faucet handles, discard paper towel. Do not use bare hands to shut off faucet as it recontaminates washed hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked in the dishwashing area by gloves, steel wool scrubber, and sponges. Handwashing sinks must be free from any objects not intended for handwashing at all times. Only items allowed are soap, paper towels, and fingernail scrubbers (if applicable). Discussed with person in charge. Items were removed from the handsink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine observed at 0 ppm. Ensure machines are showing proper concentrations according to label prior to washing. 

Dish machine chlorine sanitizer concentration observed at 0 ppm. Bucket of sanitizer under washing machine observed nearly empty. Discussed with PIC. PIC should check and ensure machine is working/sanitizer concentration is appropriate prior to washing dishes. Also discussed how chemical efficacy deteriorates over time naturally, therefore it should be changed once it is low and in-use for some time. PIC is using a 3-compartment sink in the meantime until new sanitizer is delivered. No follow up needed.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display

PIC removed bowls from prep cooler and is implementing a new process for portioning out wok items.

Also observed boxes labeled for raw chicken being used to store wrapped food and cleaning equipment. Discussed with PIC that this is not a safe practice as salmonella bacteria could potentially be transferred to these items in storage.

findings.citation_text: 3-202.15  (Pf) Food packaging on dried chili peppers and pepper is in poor condition. The containers were discarded during the inspection.  Food packaging must be in good condition so that foods are not exposed to adulteration or potential contamination. Reference 3-202.15.

findings.title: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction
findings.citation_text: 3-402.11  (P) Food establishment is serving undercooked, ready-to-eat fish that has not undergone proper parasite destruction process. The owner of the facility does not keep receipts and records for sushi fish on-site. All observed tuna is thawed and ready-to-eat. Per a phone conversation, the owner indicated the fish is received frozen. Examples of records were viewed with facility. Provide evidence/documentation that undercooked, ready-to-eat fish has been properly frozen at appropriate temperature and time to ensure parasite destruction. Reference 3-402.11.

Also, observed personal foods being stored on the second to top shelf over produce.  Store eggs and other personal foods  so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 0 ppm in bucket. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114. The facility was only using a soap and water bucket on the frontline. A sani-bucket filled with chlorine solution should be available at the front and rear of house.  4-601.11Observed four rice steamers to be soiled around the rim of the heating unit with old rice. Two steamers were in-use and two had been stored 'clean' for future use. Also, the meat slicer is observed soiled from previous use (with no current use occurring) and old, greasy paper toweling is observed within several pans used as scoops from fryers. The tongs over the lime container is soiled with a sticky red substance (pulled for cleaning).  Food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Sushi rice is observed at 75°F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).   Time as Control form was created and discussed with staff. Food should be held for four hours and then discarded.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19  (Pf) Sushi rice is out of temperature control at 75 °F. The method of Time as a Public Health Control does not have an effective written method to record the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control to the discard time. Discussed the HACCP concepts and requirement for written procedures with the person in charge. Product discarded by person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

3-304-12 Observed a portion cup being used as a scoop within ready-to-eat red pepper flakes. Removed during inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Wet wiping cloths are observed on various counters on the kitchen frontline. Cloths were removed from counters, however, a proper sani-bucket was not created until the end of the inspection. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly on-the counter and soiled with food (soup ladle and salad tossing bowl). Removed for cleaning during the inspection.  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-502.13  (C) ) Observed multiple pieces of used parchment paper on baking rack by triple sink. Paper is being used to dry coconut and fried bread crumbs. Parchment paper appears to have gone through multiple uses. Cease re-use of parchment paper. Pulled from racks during inspection. Single service articles are reused. Single service articles may not be reused. Reference 4-502.13.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-201.11  (C) A large, bare wood log is being used in the kitchen as a storage counter. The log has a deep groove down the side that allows for storage of grease and debris within the groove. Cease use of this bare wood for storage. Remove from use and replace with equipment that is durable and easily cleanable meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI standards. Reference 4-201.11.
ALSO, the glass at the sliding sushi cooler is observed cracked. Replace glass.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) and (C)  (C)  Grease and soil accumulation present on: (1) interior sides of preparation cooler lid; (2) rolling storage rack in the walk-in cooler. . Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11  (C) Observed a cell phone, windshield scrapper, and a magazine on a counter between a cutting board and plastic wrap (food preparation area). Moved items during the inspection. Areas designated for employees lockers shall be located so that food, equipment, linens, and single-service and single-use articles are protected from contamination.  Reference 6-403.11.
